CLIPORA / FEATURE

Your best replies, ready to reuse.

Keep the small pieces of writing you use every day: a helpful reply, a project update, an address or a checklist. Find the right one without rewriting it.

Build a small, useful snippet library

Use New snippet in the library to create reusable text. Give it a name that describes when you use it, such as “Design review follow-up”. Organize related clips with collections and tags.

Start with three snippets you actually need. Short, specific replies are easier to adapt than a long generic template.

Design review follow-up

Thanks for the feedback. I’ll update the draft and send the next version tomorrow.

Pin, search and paste

Pin your frequent snippets to keep them above ordinary history in quick access. Click your destination, press Ctrl + Alt + V, search the snippet’s text or name, and select it.

Use the item menu to edit, copy or delete a snippet. Unpinning changes its position; it does not delete it. Review the destination and the words before sending a reply.

Leave room for the details that change

Clipora includes placeholder snippets for reusable text with changing details. Use the snippet editor’s supported placeholder controls and review the result before pasting.

This is a picker-based workflow. Clipora does not promise that typing an abbreviation such as “;reply” will automatically expand in every app. If automatic typed-abbreviation expansion is your main requirement, evaluate a tool designed for that task.

Keep private information out of shared templates

History is encrypted locally, but a ready-to-paste reply is still visible when you open it. Keep passwords, access tokens and sensitive customer details out of reusable snippets. Pause recording before copying information you do not want retained.

Use a password-encrypted backup before moving your snippet library to another installation.

Paste the words. Leave the formatting.

A copied paragraph can bring along a font, background color or link style. Plain-text paste keeps its text while leaving the source styling behind.

Use Clipora’s password-encrypted export for a portable backup. Keep the password separately and verify the file before resetting or uninstalling the app.
